prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production pixel-art game sprite atlas, “Raccoon Professor Mari” Stories A.
Input images: Image 1 is the full user mock containing the target raccoon-kigurumi costume and cute-feral mood; Image 2 is a tighter crop of that costume; Image 3 is canonical Professor Mari identity and core pixel style; Image 4 is a montage of the four matching safari sheets for layout, scale, baseline, and action language only. Do not copy safari clothing or the mock’s card background/text.
Primary request: Create EXACTLY sixteen isolated full-body sprites of the same Professor Mari, arranged as an exact 4-column × 4-row atlas. Overall intended atlas 1024×1536, each conceptual cell 256×384. Each row is one four-beat chronological animation left-to-right. Mari is the only figure in every cell.
Identity locked in all 16 cells: adult feminine chibi Professor Mari, voluminous shoulder-length blonde curls spilling from hood, bright blue eyes, black rectangular glasses, same recognizable face and proportions as canonical reference.
Costume locked in all 16 cells: grey raccoon kigurumi onesie; hood up with raccoon ears and black eye-mask pattern on the hood face; light-grey belly panel and front zipper; one big fluffy ringed raccoon tail with alternating grey/black rings; dark-grey mitten paws with tiny claw tips; dark-grey foot paws. Cute-spooky “feral zombie” accents only: a few small tasteful fabric rips with tiny pink skin glimpses, one tiny cartoon scratch mark, small fangs only when grinning. No blood, wounds, gore, drool, or exposed anatomy.
Style/medium: crisp polished pixel art matching references, square pixel clusters, clean dark pixel outline, reduced limited palette, chibi game-sprite rendering; no smooth anime painting.
Layout/framing: EXACTLY 4 columns and 4 rows with no dividers or grid. Same character scale and same foot baseline within every cell. One complete Mari per cell. Keep ears, tail, paws, and every prop fully inside its own cell with generous transparent gutters; nothing crosses cells; no overlaps between sprites.
Row 1 — IDLE, left to right: (1) tugs both hood ears; (2) peeks playfully around her own curled tail; (3) notices one tiny bat; (4) grins with paws on hips, small fangs.
Row 2 — THINKING: (1) one claw taps chin; (2) tail swishes while pondering; (3) idea moment with one tiny lit jack-o’-lantern beside her; (4) points confidently ahead.
Row 3 — RESEARCH: (1) sniffs one old closed book; (2) reads the same book with a small magnifier; (3) scribbles abstract marks in it; (4) proudly shows the book.
Row 4 — PLANNING: (1) unrolls one map bearing only an abstract skull doodle and abstract marks; (2) studies it; (3) marks it with one claw; (4) points onward while holding rolled map.
Background: genuinely transparent alpha only.
Constraints: no scenery, no backdrop, no floor, no ground shadow, no glow, no haze, no matte, no checkerboard, no grid, no labels, no readable text, no watermark, no extra people, no duplicate body parts, no costume changes. Tiny bat and jack-o’-lantern must stay inside their cells.
